title: Design cryptographically signed repository architecture with subkey rotation
input: An enterprise wants to host a public Debian/Ubuntu APT and Fedora DNF repository. What cryptographic key hierarchy and signing workflow should be established to ensure repository authenticity while protecting the master private key?
evidence_requirements: Separation of offline master key from online repository signing subkeys
Generation of InRelease / Release.gpg for APT and repomd.xml.asc for DNF
Subkey expiration policy and periodic rotation schedule without rotating the root trusted public key

title: Diagnose client 404 and checksum mismatch during mirror synchronization
input: Users report that `apt update` intermittently fails with `Hash Sum mismatch` or `404 Not Found` when downloading packages from a newly mirrored repository. What causes this synchronization race condition and how is it prevented?
evidence_requirements: Identification of race condition where mirrors sync metadata files before package files have completed downloading
Enforcement of two-stage rsync ordering (sync pool/ first, then dists/ metadata)
Adoption of by-hash metadata layout to prevent race conditions during updates

title: Implement staged repository promotion pipeline with atomic metadata updates
input: How should software packages be promoted from CI/CD into `dev`, `staging`, and `production` repositories, and how must metadata updates be executed on production servers to prevent client-side read errors?
evidence_requirements: Implementation of staged environments (dev -> staging -> production) with automated gating tests
Promotion of identical binary packages without recompilation
Atomic replacement of repository metadata (e.g. symlink swap or directory rename) to eliminate partial-write windows

title: Analyze upgrade failures caused by unhandled conffiles and file collisions
input: During a fleet upgrade from distro version 1 to 2, hundreds of systems stall at interactive dpkg conffile prompts or fail with RPM file collision errors (`file /etc/foo conflicts between attempted installs of pkg-a and pkg-b`). How are these packaging issues audited and resolved?
evidence_requirements: Detection of unhandled configuration file changes and adoption of ucf or %config(noreplace)
Auditing for file collisions across package boundaries using lintian/rpmlint or repository queries
Resolution of file moves using Breaks/Replaces in Debian or Obsoletes/Conflicts in RPM

title: Execute emergency repository rollback without breaking client dependency caches
input: A flawed version of a critical networking utility `netfoo 3.0.0-1` was published to production, causing boot hangs. Simply deleting `netfoo 3.0.0-1` from the repo broke client updates with 404s and did not downgrade installed clients. What is the correct emergency rollback procedure?
evidence_requirements: Explanation why deleting packages from pools causes 404s and fails to downgrade clients
Execution of epoch bump / fast-forward revert package (e.g., netfoo 1:2.9.0-1 or 2.9.0-2+revert)
Repository snapshot reversion and client downgrade guidance (apt-get --allow-downgrades or dnf distro-sync)

title: Validate repository co-installability and detect broken dependencies using SAT solvers
input: Before publishing a release of 5,000 packages, how can release engineers mathematically verify that all packages are installable and that no broken dependency chains or unresolvable conflicts exist in the archive?
evidence_requirements: Execution of formal SAT solver tools (such as dose-distcheck or dose-deb-coinstall for APT)
Execution of dnf repoquery --unsolved for RPM repositories
Automated gating halting publication if broken packages or uninstallable leaves are detected
